# choices.md — the build's choices where the design is unclear or leaves a case open (J156)

The design is a reference, not a contract. Where it is unclear, or the fix list leaves a case open, the seat that meets
the case picks, records the pick here and names the test that holds it; the tests judge. One row per choice; rows are
append-only (a reversal is a new row naming the row it replaces). A choice that changes the design's text is also routed
to the fix list, and the design is corrected later from it.

Columns: **id** · **date** · **seat** · **design section** · **the choice** · **the reason** · **the test that holds it**.

Clipper2's booleans run through its **double** API (precision 10⁻³ cm) and are snapped by the kernel's `snap`: its integer API truncates every new intersection point toward zero — up to 1 cm on each axis, measured on this machine — which put the two oracles 0.95 cm/cm apart on dense xor cases, where §3.2 (1) rounds to the nearest lattice point (0.089 cm/cm after the change). The library's missing declaration is a local `declare module` typing its default export as returning `unknown`, narrowed to the adapter's own interfaces; no library type reaches an exported signature (C-0124 (2), N-15). (2) *Fill rules on polygon-clipping*, which has no fill parameter and reads a self-crossing ring by the non-zero rule: non-zero — an operand's rings joined into one ring by doubled bridges from its first ring's first vertex (winding numbers add; each bridge, traversed once each way, adds none); even-odd — the XOR of the operand's simple rings (exact test on the kernel's `orient2d`) and of the fan triangles of each non-simple ring (crossing parity adds over any split of the boundary into closed paths). Every polygon-clipping call runs under the four exact quarter turns of the plane in turn (identity first), the result turned back, because its sweep in doubles throws on some near-degenerate inputs; only when all four throw is the case a typed oracle failure. (3) *Faces after snapping:* a face is a connected piece of the region's interior: the snapped rings are canonicalised by polygon-clipping's non-zero union and its output polygons of positive area counted — so two faces touching at a point count two however a library wrote them, a hole touching its outline counts none (the loop count of the representation is the fallback when the canonicalisation throws). | C-0161 | 2026-10-04 | build/M0-k-01 (M0-k-01) | §13.1 (1) (random inputs: concave, holed, thin, near-collinear, self-touching, snapped, duplicated-vertex, ≥ 300-vertex and zero-area polygons and chains), §13.2 (seed i of a family `H32("bcity/<rung>/<water>/<i>")`, rehashed by V12 §2.4's rule), §13.6 (2) (`H32`), §13.8 (10⁴ PR, 10⁶ nightly per primitive), §3.4 (`warp(tx, field: DisplacementField, …)`), §7.1 (the brush kernels), §16 M0 (b) (curved, round-joined, triangular, C-shaped and holed faces), §4.6 step 8 (F-CUT on random concave and holed faces), §1.1 (CITY's frame), C-0057, C-0107 — item M0-k-01's readings where the design leaves a case open; **refines C-0057 (the per-family seeds); supersedes nothing** | (1) **Bounds.** Every coordinate passes the kernel's `snap`; the default range is snap's whole range, |v| ≤ 2²³ − 1; a caller's `limitCm` is an integer in [65 536, 2²³ − 1] (room for every class's construction), else a RangeError. (2) **Exact construction, integer draws.** Shapes whose validity is promised are built on the lattice with exact integer tests, never by snapping a valid double shape: a star ring is k directions, one per angular sector about a lattice centre, sorted exactly by angle and kept only when every angular gap is below π, so it is simple and counter-clockwise by construction; radii are ≥ 5 % of the circumradius R and R ≥ 64 cm × k, so the k directions survive rounding distinct and in order (exactly k vertices). The arbitraries draw only integers (sizes log-uniform by octave, per-mille shares, positions as fractions of the room left) and map them, so every shrink maps to a valid shape and shrinking moves to the smallest sizes; trigonometry goes through `dmath` (M0-d-03, landed at wave 2), so a seed gives the same shapes on every host. Touching and thin shapes are rotated by unimodular lattice maps (a symmetry of the square times shears), which keep every incidence exactly; thin strips take only a vertical shear, which keeps them thin. (3) **The interface's form.** Each `arb` member is a factory with optional options, fast-check's own convention (`arb.polygon()`, `arb.faceSet('curved', { scale: 'plot' })`); a class arbitrary takes `{ shape: 'polygon' | 'chain' }`. Beyond the listed members the builds' families with no listed name are `arb.duplicated`, `arb.zeroArea`, `arb.large` and `arb.stroke`. `arb.faceSet(kind)` draws one face; a set is n draws from one seed family. (4) **The classes, measured.** The registry `FUZZ_CLASSES` holds each of the nine classes for polygons and for chains with the arbitrary that draws it and an exact classifier that recognises a member from the shape alone: concave — a vertex turning against the ring's orientation, a chain turning both ways; thin — mean width (twice the area over the boundary length, a chain closed by its last edge) at most 5 % of the bounding-box diagonal; near-collinear — a vertex 0 < d ≤ 2 cm off its neighbours' line, its projection strictly inside their segment; self-touching — a vertex on an edge it does not end; snapped — at least three vertices within 3 cm of one circle about their mean (rectangles and regular n-gons are cyclic, snap moves a vertex ≤ √2 / 2 cm); duplicated-vertex — two consecutive vertices equal; ≥ 300 vertices; zero-area — an exact twice-area of 0, a chain on one line. *Holed* does not apply to chains (a chain bounds no area). The coverage table samples 200 values per row from seed 0 of `fuzz/coverage/<class>/<shape>`; a class's own arbitrary must be recognised on all 200, the generic `arb.polygon()` / `arb.chain()` on ≥ 60 % / ≥ 50 % as concave, `arb.regularSnapped` on ≥ 90 % (a tiny radius can fold a snapped shape). (5) **Faces.** Block scale is a circumradius of 30–300 m, plot scale 4–30 m (the S11 workload's plots, C-0107); every face lies inside CITY's 5 km frame (§1.1). Curved: 3–6 corners, sides bowed by a half-sine of −12 % … +25 % of the chord; round-joined: 3–7 corners each replaced by a quadratic join over 10–40 % of its half-sides; triangular: three corners with angular gaps of 72°–168° about the centre and 0–12 kerb vertices per side; C-shaped: an annular sector, inner radius 35–65 % of R, span 200°–300°, arcs every 4°–12°, checked by the exact simplicity test; holed: a star outline with 1–2 disjoint holes; and `concave` for F-CUT's random faces (5–14 vertices, ≥ 1 reflex). (6) **Fields.** §3.4 names `DisplacementField` without a shape and M0-a-13 (wave 8) builds `warp`, so the field is the test kit's own `FuzzField` — `displacement(x, y)` in cm (doubles), exactly 0 at and beyond `radiusCm`, bounded by `maxDisplacementCm`, with its `region` as a snapped 16-gon — and its consumer adapts it; the kinds are §7.1's pointwise kernels `displace`, `liquify`, `swirl`, `bloat`, `pinch`, `jitter` (`bloat` / `pinch` read pointwise about the brush centre); `relax` and `equalize` read a cell's ring and stay the edit layer's. (7) **Seeds.** `seedFamily(name, i)` = H32("<name>/<i>"), §13.2's form with the family name before the index (so §13.6 (2)'s check vectors hold for `d5/…` names), a function of (name, i) alone; V12 §2.4's collision rehash is not applied — it serves the B-CITY seed families, which are M1's (the item's defers), and volume 12 is not an M0 read. `fuzzParams(name, i)` gives `{ seed }`, the family seed as fast-check's int32, unless PLAT_FUZZ_SEED fixed the global seed (a replay wins); `fuzzRuns()` reads PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS as the setup file does, for a runner outside vitest. (8) **The generators' own tests** run min(PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS, 2 000) cases per property (quadratic checks on ≥ 300-vertex shapes min(…, 100)): their claims name no size, and the tier sizes 10⁴ / 10⁶ are B-FUZZ's per kernel primitive (§13.8), drawn from these generators by M0-k-04. (9) **Holes** sit in fan triangles (pᵢ, pᵢ₊₁, c) of the star outline, two fans apart, so no two holes meet; a vertex contact is one lattice point of the closed side (an outline vertex or a point inside the side), an edge contact a stretch a′b′ of it; holes touching each other are M0-k-02's constructive class, not drawn here. | The design names the classes, the tier sizes and the seed form but not the generators' shapes, scales, options, field type or seed string; an exact construction keeps every shrink valid and every claim checkable; a classifier independent of the construction makes the coverage table a measurement. | `packages/testkit/test/fuzz/lattice.test.ts` (every arbitrary yields only coordinates snap accepts; shrinking terminates on every arbitrary, at a value it could have drawn); `contacts.test.ts` (the holed polygons' holes inside the outer ring with each stated contact; the self-touching chains and rings touch and never cross; negative controls); `seeds.test.ts` (the seed family is a function of (name, i) alone; §13.6 (2)'s check vectors; refusals; `fuzzParams`, `fuzzRuns`); `coverage.test.ts` (the coverage table printed, naming the nine classes for polygons and chains, every floor met; the classifiers on members and non-members); `shapes.test.ts` (each arbitrary's stated shape, counts, fields, face kinds and scales, refusals, one seed one sample). |

(2) **The graph is the dual of the Delaunay triangles inside the sampled boundary.** Every piece must be an edge of the triangulation; a parity walk from the hull (outside, or inside across a piece on the hull) flips across each piece — a site pair two rings share counted twice, the even–odd rule's reading — and marks every triangle inside or out; one arc per Delaunay edge between two inside triangles; centres within 1 mm one node (union along those arcs, only between centres inside the face — C-0172 (6)'s guard kept); self-loops dropped, parallel arcs one. (3) **Pruned by clearance from the leaves only.** Leaves are taken from a min-heap by clearance (ties by triangle index); a leaf's arc goes when it is prunable — each of its Voronoi edges separates two sites of one ring lying no farther apart along it (the shorter way round) than π × the edge's least clearance (C-0172 (5)'s ratio: a corner of about 79° or more leaves no branch, a sharper one keeps its bisector; sites on different rings: never) —, when it meets a ring (tested under half a step + 1 cm of clearance), or when the leaf's centre is not inside the face; the far end may then become a leaf. Removing a leaf never splits the graph and never opens a hole's loop. A graph pruned whole keeps its last node (a square's centre, its node of greatest clearance); a ring set whose inside triangles give no arc at all is its one inside node of greatest clearance; a bad node or arc not reachable from a leaf is dropped afterwards and the leaves pruned again. (4) **`MedialAxis` gains `refined`** (the samples the refinement added) **and `resolved`**: true when the refinement ended with no piece stuck and no bound reached, every piece is an edge of the triangulation with a consistent parity, and nothing had to be dropped except from a leaf — then (2) and (3) hold: connected, one independent cycle per hole.
